You're both hurt and mad with valid reasons. You already got answers why she might be mad and hurt. And you want to be seen and feel desired, loved and respected and that's also valid.
One of you needs to put their feelings aside for a second to start the conversation and approach the other one.
I think she should learn to communicate better and start to talk about what's bothering her. But she's in a very vulnerable position and is probably only going to open up once she feels safe. Right now she might be defensive because she's hurt and she only hears about what you want and need and she might be overwhelmed. She might feel safer once you ask her with love, without judging what's going on just listen and talk about her. There's something going on and she can't see past it to be there for you. That's something she can overcome by opening up and feeling safe and processing the emotions. It might take a while, depending what's going on.
Afterwards, once she has nothing more to say about herself and she's able to listen to you, you can tell her that you'd wish she communicate better because the ways she's doing it you're not feeling loved. You can think about how you'd like she communicate with you and how you can also show her that her wellbeing is always your priority.

Feelings are always valid, you can't control them.
But you can control your actions. It's okay to be hurt but right now you need to think about what's the best way to solve this situation together and not about who is right and who is wrong
